record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: Among all unicyclic graphs on n vertices, is the maximum graph energy achieved by the cycle Cn for n ≤ 7 and for n = 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, while for all remaining values of n the maximum is achieved by the lollipop graph Lol(n,6), obtained by joining a cycle C6 to a path P(n−6) with a single edge from a cycle vertex to an endpoint of the path?

evidence.page: Energy of a graph, HTML lines 1262-1268
evidence.quote: In this study, the particular case of unicyclic graphs was considered... The following conjecture was stated. Conjecture 5.2... Among unicyclic graphs on n vertices the cycle C_n has maximal energy if n ≤ 7 and n = 9, 10, 11, 13 and 15. For all other values of n the unicyclic graph with maximum energy is the lollipop Lol_{n,6}.

evidence.page: Energy of a graph, HTML lines 1279-1283
evidence.quote: Again, in another paper, Huo et al. (2011) solved completely the problem to get Theorem 5.5... Among all unicyclic graphs on n vertices, the cycle C_n has maximal energy if n ≤ 7 but n ≠ 4, and n = 9, 10, 11, 13 and 15; Lol_{4,3} has maximal energy if n = 4. For all other values of n, the unicyclic graph with maximal energy is Lol_{n,6}.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let G be a simple graph with adjacency matrix A(G), and let λ_1, λ_2, …, λ_n denote the eigenvalues of A(G). The energy of G is defined by E(G) = Σ_{i=1}^{n} |λ_i|. A unicyclic graph is a connected graph containing exactly one cycle. For integers n ≥ 6 and 3 ≤ g ≤ n, the lollipop graph Lol(n,g) is obtained from a cycle C_g and a path P_{n-g} on n-g vertices by joining a single vertex of C_g to an endpoint of P_{n-g} by an edge (so Lol(n,g) has n vertices and exactly one cycle, of length g).\n\nDetermine, among all unicyclic graphs on n vertices, which graph has the maximum energy. Specifically, decide whether the following statement is true: the cycle C_n attains the maximum energy among unicyclic graphs on n vertices precisely for n ∈ {3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 15}, while for all remaining values of n ≥ 4 (with n ≠ 4) the maximum is attained by the lollipop Lol(n,6).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture was completely resolved by Huo, Ji, and Li (2011). The maximum-energy unicyclic graph on n vertices is C_n for n ≤ 7 with n ≠ 4 and for n ∈ {9, 10, 11, 13, 15}; Lol(4,3) is the maximum for n = 4; and Lol(n,6) is the maximum for all remaining n. Thus the originally stated conjecture is correct except for the small case n = 4.

status_evidence.title: Solution of a conjecture on the maximal energy of unicyclic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Huo, Ji, Li (2011) proved that for n ≥ 7 the maximum-energy unicyclic graph is the lollipop Lol(n,6) (with the listed exceptions where C_n is maximal).
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture characterizing the maximum-energy unicyclic graph has been proved.
